key_insight: Methylammonium lead iodide perovskite thin films exhibit alternating ferroelectric polarization domains with ~90 nm width, indicating intrinsic ferroic behavior.
engineering_relevance: Local ferroelectric polarization may influence charge extraction and therefore impact perovskite solar-cell performance and device optimization.
method: Piezoresponse Force Microscopy (PFM) in vertical and horizontal modes to map domain polarization
High-resolution photo-conductive AFM under illumination to observe charge-carrier extraction patterns
Correlation with AFM and Kelvin Probe Force Microscopy to validate domain-related surface properties
evidence_signal: The abstract reports alternating polarization domains and matching illumination-induced charge extraction patterns, consistent with piezoelectric/ferroelectric behavior.
watch_item: The observations are local-surface measurements on thin films, so translating domain behavior directly to full-device performance requires caution.
paper_title: Ferroelectric domains in methylammonium lead iodide perovskite thin-films
